title: Maintaining Air Quality: Application and Carbon Cycle - Worksheet 2
topic: Application of Air Quality Knowledge and the Carbon Cycle
subject: Pure Chemistry

questions.question: A city introduces a congestion charge to reduce vehicle use. Which air pollutant is most likely to decrease as a result?
options: Sulfur dioxide only
Carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter
Ozone only
Methane only
questions.explanation: Reducing vehicle numbers directly lowers emissions from combustion: CO (incomplete combustion), NOₓ (high-temperature N₂+O₂ reaction), and particulates (soot from diesel/petrol).

questions.question: In the carbon cycle, which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
options: Respiration
Combustion of fossil fuels
Photosynthesis
Decomposition of organic matter
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Plants absorb CO₂ from the atmosphere to make glucose, acting as a carbon sink. Respiration and combustion release CO₂.

questions.question: Which human activity has most significantly increased atmospheric CO₂ levels since the Industrial Revolution?
options: Deforestation only
Burning of fossil fuels
Agriculture and livestock
Volcanic eruptions
questions.explanation: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon stored underground for millions of years as CO₂. This anthropogenic input exceeds natural carbon cycle fluxes, causing atmospheric CO₂ to rise.

questions.question: How do oceans help regulate atmospheric carbon dioxide levels?
options: Oceans produce CO₂ through respiration only
Oceans absorb CO₂, forming carbonic acid and carbonate ions
Oceans release CO₂ when water temperature decreases
Oceans have no significant role in the carbon cycle
questions.explanation: CO₂ dissolves in seawater: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻ ⇌ 2H⁺ + CO₃²⁻. Oceans absorb ~30% of anthropogenic CO₂, but this causes ocean acidification, harming marine life.

questions.question: A student claims that planting more trees will completely solve global warming. Which statement best evaluates this claim?
options: Correct, because trees absorb all human CO₂ emissions
Partially correct, but trees alone cannot offset current emission rates
Incorrect, because trees release more CO₂ than they absorb
Correct, because forests also produce oxygen
questions.explanation: While trees absorb CO₂, current global emissions (~40 Gt CO₂/year) far exceed what new forests can sequester. Mitigation requires both carbon sinks AND drastic emission reductions.

questions.question: Which equation represents the overall process of respiration?
options: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O
CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
questions.explanation: Respiration is the reverse of photosynthesis: glucose is oxidised with oxygen to release energy, producing CO₂ and water. This occurs in plants, animals and microorganisms.

questions.question: Why is methane (CH₄) considered a more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide?
options: Methane is present in much higher concentrations
Methane absorbs infrared radiation more effectively per molecule
Methane remains in the atmosphere longer than CO₂
Methane is produced only by human activities
questions.explanation: Per molecule, CH₄ is ~28-36× more effective at trapping heat than CO₂ over 100 years. However, CO₂ is more concerning overall due to its much higher concentration and longer atmospheric lifetime.

questions.question: Which process in the carbon cycle involves the breakdown of dead organisms by microorganisms?
options: Photosynthesis
Combustion
Decomposition
Sedimentation
questions.explanation: Decomposers (bacteria, fungi) break down dead organic matter, releasing CO₂ through respiration. This returns carbon to the atmosphere, completing part of the carbon cycle.

questions.question: A power station uses flue gas desulfurisation. If 1000 kg of SO₂ is treated with excess calcium carbonate, what mass of calcium sulfite (CaSO₃) is produced? [Mr: SO₂=64, CaSO₃=120]
options: 640 kg
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ + SO₂ → CaSO₃ + CO₂. Moles SO₂ = 1000×1000/64 = 15625 mol. Moles CaSO₃ = 15625 mol (1:1 ratio). Mass CaSO₃ = 15625 × 120 = 1,875,000 g = 1875 kg.

questions.question: Which statement about the greenhouse effect is correct?
options: It is caused only by human activities
It is a natural process that keeps Earth warm enough for life
It can be eliminated by removing all CO₂ from the atmosphere
It is the same as ozone layer depletion
questions.explanation: The natural greenhouse effect traps heat via greenhouse gases (CO₂, H₂O, CH₄), keeping Earth ~33°C warmer than it would be otherwise. Human activities enhance this effect, causing global warming.

questions.question: In a catalytic converter, which metal is primarily used to catalyse the reduction of nitrogen oxides?
options: Iron
Platinum
Rhodium
Copper
questions.explanation: Rhodium is particularly effective for reducing NOₓ to N₂. Platinum and palladium are better for oxidising CO and hydrocarbons. Modern converters use all three metals for complete emission control.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how carbon is stored in fossil fuels?
options: Carbon is absorbed directly from the atmosphere by coal and oil
Ancient organic matter was buried and transformed under heat and pressure over millions of years
Fossil fuels are formed from inorganic carbon compounds in the Earth's crust
Carbon in fossil fuels comes from volcanic emissions
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels formed from ancient plants and microorganisms that were buried, then subjected to heat and pressure over geological time. The carbon was originally fixed from CO₂ via photosynthesis.

questions.question: A student sets up an experiment to show that plants absorb CO₂. Which observation would support this claim?
options: The plant grows taller in the dark
Limewater turns milky when air from around the plant is bubbled through it
Limewater remains clear when air from around a plant in light is bubbled through it
The plant releases oxygen bubbles in water
questions.explanation: Limewater (Ca(OH)₂) turns milky with CO₂ due to CaCO₃ formation. If air from around a photosynthesising plant does NOT turn limewater milky, it suggests CO₂ has been absorbed by the plant.

questions.question: Which mitigation strategy addresses both air pollution and climate change?
options: Installing taller smokestacks
Switching from coal to natural gas for electricity
Using electrostatic precipitators
Adding lead scavengers to petrol
questions.explanation: Natural gas (CH₄) produces less CO₂ per unit energy than coal, and emits negligible SO₂ and particulates. This reduces both greenhouse gas emissions and local air pollutants.

questions.question: Which process in the carbon cycle transfers carbon from the atmosphere to the lithosphere (rocks)?
options: Photosynthesis
Formation of sedimentary rocks like limestone
Volcanic eruptions
Respiration
questions.explanation: Marine organisms use dissolved CO₂ to form CaCO₃ shells. When they die, shells accumulate on the ocean floor, forming limestone over millions of years, storing carbon in the lithosphere.

questions.question: Why is it difficult to completely eliminate nitrogen oxide emissions from vehicle engines?
options: Nitrogen oxides are produced only during cold starts
High combustion temperatures cause N₂ and O₂ from air to react
Catalytic converters cannot function at high temperatures
Nitrogen oxides are added to fuel to improve performance
questions.explanation: At high engine temperatures (>1300°C), atmospheric N₂ and O₂ react: N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO. This thermal NOₓ formation is inherent to high-temperature combustion, making complete elimination challenging.

questions.question: Which of the following is a limitation of using biofuels to reduce air pollution?
options: Biofuels produce more CO₂ than fossil fuels when burned
Growing biofuel crops may compete with food production and cause deforestation
Biofuels cannot be used in existing vehicle engines
Biofuels release more sulfur dioxide than diesel
questions.explanation: While biofuels are renewable and can be carbon-neutral, large-scale production may require clearing forests or using agricultural land, potentially increasing net emissions and affecting food security.

questions.question: In the carbon cycle, which reservoir contains the largest amount of carbon?
options: Atmosphere
Oceans
Fossil fuels
Living biomass
questions.explanation: Oceans contain ~38,000 Gt of carbon (mostly as dissolved inorganic carbon), far exceeding atmosphere (~750 Gt), fossil fuels (~4000 Gt), or living biomass (~560 Gt).

questions.question: A city measures air quality and finds high levels of ground-level ozone. Which combination of pollutants is most likely responsible?
options: SO₂ and particulate matter
NOₓ and volatile organic compounds in sunlight
CO and lead compounds
CO₂ and methane
questions.explanation: Ground-level (tropospheric) ozone is a secondary pollutant formed when NOₓ and VOCs react in sunlight. It is a key component of photochemical smog and causes respiratory problems.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the carbon cycle before and after the Industrial Revolution?
options: The natural carbon cycle was in perfect balance before humans
Human activities have added a new flux of carbon from lithosphere to atmosphere
Photosynthesis rates have decreased globally since industrialisation
Ocean absorption of CO₂ has stopped completely
questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels transfers carbon that was stored in the lithosphere (as coal, oil, gas) into the atmosphere as CO₂. This anthropogenic flux disrupts the natural carbon cycle balance.
